sections.h2: Where is Archuleta County, Colorado, and what is it like?
sections.html:
Archuleta County is a mountain county in southwest Colorado on the New Mexico line, with Pagosa Springs as its county seat. It is the county's largest town and its only incorporated municipality. The Colorado legislature created the county on April 14, 1885, out of western Conejos County, and named it for Jose Manuel Archuleta and his son Antonio D. Archuleta, then a state senator.

The county covers 1,356 square miles, almost all land, and borders Mineral, Rio Grande, Conejos, Hinsdale and La Plata counties in Colorado and Rio Arriba and San Juan counties in New Mexico. Rivers and creeks include the San Juan, Piedra, Rio Blanco, Rio Chama, Little Navajo and Stollsteimer.

The county had 13,359 residents in the 2020 census, up from 826 in 1890 and 9,898 in 2000. The 2025 estimate is 14,306. Median household income was $55,658 in 2020 dollars, and about 9.4 percent of residents were below the poverty line.

sections.h2: What is Pagosa Springs known for, and how does the land shape local housing?
sections.html:
Pagosa Springs takes its name from a system of sulfur springs that Wikipedia says includes the world's deepest geothermal hot spring. The town sits at about 7,100 feet on the Western Slope, and the San Juan River flows through its middle. It is roughly 47 miles east of Durango.

About 65 percent of the land in Archuleta County is San Juan National Forest, the Weminuche and South San Juan wilderness areas, or Southern Ute reservation land. That leaves a limited supply of private building land. Pagosa Springs itself had 1,571 residents in 2020 and 964 housing units, 33.9 percent of which were vacant at the census.

Geothermal water even heats some downtown buildings. In the 1980s the town received federal Department of Energy funding to drill two wells for that purpose. A seller whose property uses geothermal heat or a private well and septic should say so, because buyers in a mountain county ask about utilities early.

sections.h2: How have floods affected Pagosa Springs property?
sections.html:
The San Juan River has flooded the town more than once. In October 1911 a flood destroyed the water pipeline and every bridge in the county, including those across the river, and washed out the railroad. On October 11, 2025, heavy rain made the river overflow again, damaged several bridges and a sewer line, and closed part of U.S. Highway 160, which is the main road through town.

Residents of Hermosa Street, San Juan Street and areas east of Hot Springs Boulevard were evacuated in 2025, and the Ross Aragon Community Center was opened as an evacuation center. A house in or near the river corridor may face flood questions from buyers, lenders and insurers, and a cash buyer does not need any of those approvals to close.

If your property was damaged, keep photos, repair receipts and any insurance claim records. Those documents help any buyer, cash or otherwise, price the work still to be done.

sections.h2: When is Archuleta County property tax due?
sections.html:
Archuleta County bills follow the statewide schedule: first half by the last day of February, second half by June 15, or the full amount by April 30. Those dates come from C.R.S. 39-10-104.5. Late amounts carry interest of one percent per month, and part of a month counts as a whole month.

The Archuleta County Treasurer mailed 2026 tax notices on January 30, 2026, and asks owners who had not received one by February 13 to call. Owners can preview and pay online through the treasurer's portal and can ask for e-statements on the Address Change and E-Notice Form.

PaymentDue date
First halfLast day of February
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Payments with no postmark that arrive within five days of the due date are credited as of the due date. Totals under $25 must be paid in full by April 30.

sections.h2: Who values property and who collects tax in Archuleta County?
sections.html:
The assessor sets value and the treasurer collects the money. The Archuleta County Treasurer says the office does not set tax amounts, and the assessor says it does not levy taxes. The treasurer is elected to a four-year term, and Elsa P. White took office in 2019.

Both offices have moved to 305 Village Drive in Pagosa Springs and keep hours Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am to 5:00 pm. The Treasurer's phone is 970-264-8325 and the Assessor's is 970-264-8310. Mailing addresses are P.O. Box 790 for the Treasurer and P.O. Box 1089 for the Assessor, both in Pagosa Springs, CO 81147.

The Assessor posts these assessment rates:

Property typeAssessment rate
Residential6.95% of market value
Multi-family6.80%
Vacant land29%
Agricultural26.40%
Lodging26.40%
Commercial and personal property29% of actual value

The assessor must mail a notice of valuation by May 1 each year. In even-numbered years the value appears on the tax bill.

sections.h2: What is the Archuleta County tax lien sale and how long can an owner redeem?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes can be sold as a lien to an investor, and the owner keeps the right to redeem. The county's 2026 sale opened for research and bidding on October 1, 2026 and closed on November 5, 2026, with winning bidders making a 10 percent deposit by ACH by October 29.

  • Certificates from the current year's sale earn 13 percent.
  • Redeemed certificates earn 4.5 percent over the Federal Reserve Discount Rate as of September 2.
  • The county says the majority of properties are redeemed.
  • A buyer can apply for a Treasurer's Deed up to three years after the sale if the lien is still unredeemed.
  • Liens expire and are cancelled after seven years.
  • If the owner does not pay the following year's taxes by July 1, the buyer is notified and may pay them, and that amount is added to the lien.

That stack of added interest is why owners with a delinquent Archuleta County house do well to act early. State law also requires the treasurer to mail a delinquency notice by September 1 with at least fifteen days to pay.

sections.h2: Can I sell my Archuleta County house with taxes due?
sections.html:
Yes. Unpaid tax and interest are paid from the sale at closing, and the title company asks the Treasurer for a payoff. Selling before a lien sale, or before a Treasurer's Deed application, can end the problem on your terms.

With so much of the county in public land, private houses are a small share of what exists. We buy Archuleta County houses as-is, so deferred work does not have to be fixed before closing. Call the Treasurer at 970-264-8325 for a payoff figure first.

faqs.q: When is the first half of Archuleta County property tax due?
faqs.a: The last day of February under C.R.S. 39-10-104.5. The second half is due June 15 and a full payment is due April 30.

faqs.q: Where is the Archuleta County Treasurer?
faqs.a: 305 Village Drive, Pagosa Springs, CO 81147. The office is open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, and the phone is 970-264-8325.

faqs.q: What is the residential assessment rate in Archuleta County?
faqs.a: The Assessor lists 6.95 percent of market value for residential property.

faqs.q: How long before a Treasurer's Deed can be applied for?
faqs.a: Up to three years after the lien sale, if the lien is still unredeemed, according to the Treasurer's lien sale summary.

faqs.q: Does Archuleta County have more than one town?
faqs.a: No. Pagosa Springs is the county seat and the only incorporated municipality in the county.

faqs.q: Can I sell if the house flooded?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so repairs are not required before the sale. Keep any repair records and insurance paperwork to share.
